questions: How many devices did you measure, and how many showed the high-field supercurrent? Your SI answers this for devices (GH1 and GH2 of GH1 to GH4, plus one non-moiré junction, SI pp. 33 and 34); could you add the number of cooldowns and datasets, and square it with "multiple additional devices" on p. 3?

Why were the others set aside? Your SI gives junction length as the reason for GH3 and GH4 (SI p. 33). Were other junctions on these stacks fabricated and not measured, and what made GH1 the main device?

Which ranges of density, field and temperature did you measure beyond those in Fig. 2a and Fig. S13a, and at which densities besides n/ns ∼ 1.8 (GH1) and n/ns = 1.6 (GH2) did you take high-field interference patterns?

What does the second-best dataset look like? GH2 (SI Section F) answers this at the device level; could you also show a high-field pocket of GH1 from another density range, for example near n/ns ∼ 2.2 or below 1.5?

How was the 3447 Ω series resistance obtained (SI p. 19), was it checked at high field and in each cooldown, and could you show Fig. 2a before subtraction, together with the threshold that marks a region as superconducting in Fig. 3e and the 20 mS cutoff of Fig. S18?
Could you reconstruct the current density across the width, as in Fig. S9c, from a high-field pattern such as Fig. 2c or Fig. S11, to tell bulk trajectories from Andreev states near the edges?

Two numbers disagree with others in the text: the single-mode limit reads IQ = e∆/h ∼ 106 ± 2 nA on p. 5 and ∼ 53 ± 1 nA on SI p. 31 (with ∆ ∼ 1.4 meV, e∆/h is about 54 nA), and SI p. 20 gives n/ns ∼ ±2.7 at 6.0 × 10^12 cm^-2, while your moiré formula with θ = 0.21° gives ns ≈ 2.5 × 10^12 cm^-2 and so n/ns ≈ 2.4. Which values are right, and which IQ did you compare with the 48 ± 2 nA of Fig. 2b?
